w:r.w:t: following instructions apply for the formatting of the report.
All tables must have a number and a title in Times New Roman Font of size 10,
, which should be displayed above the table. All figures must have a number and a caption in Times New Roman Font of size 10,
, which should be displayed below the figure.
letter of only the first word capitalized

Use IEEE referencing style. At the place in the document where you want to cite, use a number in square brackets [_]. In the references section, provide the full reference of the work. The complete IEEE referencing guide is available at:
Final year project report submitted in partial
of requirement for degree of Bachelors of Science in
The project report titled “<Project Title>” is submitted in partial fulfillment of the degree of Bachelors of Science in

It is declared that this is an original work done by the team members listed below, under the guidance of our supervisor “<supervisor name>”. No part of this project and its report is plagiarized from anywhere, and any help taken from previous work is cited properly.
No part of the work reported here is submitted in fulfillment of requirement for any other degree/ qualification in any institute of learning.
Use the auto-generated Table of Contents feature in Word for easier navigation.

Write a brief summary of the problem, proposed solution, methods used, results, scope, and future directions. Abstract should not exceed one page, and is usually written as one paragraph. It should be a standalone summary of the project report without any references, and should be easily understandable. No abbreviations should be used in the abstract.

Write a brief overview of the project and the background information required to understand different parts of it. Context for the project and reason for its selection should be provided in this section. Use as simplified language as you can (without technical terms and details) so that anyone with some basic knowledge is able to understand.

It should include the problem statement, context, aims and objectives of the project, and some overview of the solution/ criteria for completion. Provide a summary of the report structure and a brief outline of the chapters to come.
Provide a clear purpose for this SRS document. Highlight the objectives and the problem it aims to solve in an industrial context.
Explain the goals, key functionalities, and industrial applications of the project. Avoid technical jargon; use simple language.
Include a list of terms, acronyms, and abbreviations used in the document with their explanations. For example:
List all references in IEEE format. Ensure proper citation for all materials referenced.
Provide an overview of the document structure. Mention what each section will cover briefly.

Provide the project’s background in light of the literature studied. Do not go into too much detail for any one previously done project. All work referred to in the literature review must be related to the project and its scope.

Literature review can refer to work from journals, articles, or any other academic literature available. If recent literature is available, which is very closely related to the work being done in the current project, then it should always be included. It should also include references to the work from which the current project is derived. It provides evidence of the significance of the project being done.
This section will contain the most number of references, as it will mostly only consist of description of previous work done in the scope, and its relation to the current project being reported.
At the end of the chapter, relate the literature discussed with the current project and develop context for your project in light of it.
Discuss general factors affecting the system such as user characteristics, constraints, assumptions, and dependencies.
Specify the required hardware, software, and operating environments for the project.
Describe how this product relates to other existing systems or products.
List the high-level features of the system and provide a brief explanation for each.
Software Process Model, Data Flow Diagram, Object Models, Use Cases, Block Diagrams, Flow-charts, or pseudo code etc
. Please note that while the literature review will review the already available techniques, the methodology must be specific to the project.
The complete solution must be discussed here in detail with supporting evidence like
figures, tables, flow charts and/or chunks of code.
should include the process explained in sufficient details so that the project may be re-implemented from the information available.
Clearly define the functional requirements. Use bullet points or tables for clarity. For example:
The system shall allow users to log in securely.
The system shall generate reports based on input data
Specify requirements such as performance, security, scalability, usability, reliability, and compliance with industrial standards.
Provide detailed DFDs for the system processes.
Illustrate system interactions using use case diagrams.
Show the database schema using an Entity-Relationship Diagram.
Visualize workflows and processes with sequence and activity diagrams.
Describe the system’s user interfaces, focusing on usability.
List the hardware components and their specifications.
Describe the APIs, libraries, and third-party software used.
Detail the communication protocols and formats employed.
Highlight real-world constraints such as cost, time, and technological barriers
List assumptions about the system and dependencies.
Assumption: Internet connectivity will be stable.
Dependency: System relies on high-resolution video feeds.
The Remaining Work section provides a roadmap for the tasks that still need to be completed before the project can be considered finished.

List Outstanding Tasks: Enumerate the specific tasks that are yet to be completed. Be clear and concise in describing each task. You may categorize them based on priority, dependencies, or the stage of completion.

Status of Each Task: For each remaining task, provide a brief status update. Mention whether it's in progress, pending, or if any obstacles have been encountered. This gives readers an understanding of the current state of affairs.

Timeline and Milestones: Include a timeline for completing the remaining tasks. Specify milestones or deadlines for each outstanding task. This helps in setting expectations and provides a structured approach to completing the work.
List pending tasks, their current status, and expected timelines. Example:
Task 1: Finalize system architecture (In progress, expected completion: MM/DD/YYYY).
